faq.q: What is a good day 30 retention rate for a social app?
faq.a: The median is 12% at day 30, three times the 4% cross-industry average, with strong performers at 15% to 20%. Social is the strongest retaining category published, because the value is other people rather than features.

faq.q: Why are dating apps different from social apps?
faq.a: Because success removes the user. A dating product that works loses its best-served customers, which no other category has to plan for. No published benchmark separates dating from social, so the 12% median flatters dating and understates community products.

faq.q: Does a high retention rate mean a social app is healthy?
faq.a: Not on its own. A social product can retain a shrinking group intensely while failing to add anyone, and a cohort table showing high retention with falling new-cohort size is a product in decline with a flattering curve.

unique_value_statement: Names the incentive inversion in dating that every blended social benchmark hides — a working dating product loses the users it serves best — and shows how a high retention median can describe a shrinking base.
